BRIEF.md SHA256 86D66542BFCAC53D74499BF8808EDC2855406B026610452D9F42363615A668E6
Implement a dormant controller-to-child namespace connection in a fresh scratch directory chosen by root. Stop after issuing an exact child-local lease over the five selected, verified buffers. Constructor, options, VAD, PCM and inference work stay outside this unit.

The controller startup unit is accepted at commit 9c87ec216768fcd7b86cc97c9c8779f1fdafa49a: both guarded copies passed 81/0/0 with 48 passing subtests. Its proof is docs/library/proof/startup-authority-fake81-2026-09-14, seal prefix 34b8e9f7. This is root-reported qualification, not a new observation by this plan. Derive the accepted adapter6482b782 and protocol86977e0d, plus the original namespace/adoption/transport sources bound in SOURCE-INPUTS.json. Connection01 is rejected source context only; none of its 15 proposed cases ran.

Make five connected source changes. Preserve all existing generated methods, accepted test bodies and public real-entry refusals.

1. Extend the accepted adapter with a separate post-consumption validation method. Existing `_consume_controller_startup(startup, permit, session)` takes an exact `OwnedSession` once; `_validate_controller_startup(...)` intentionally requires RESERVED, token.worker=None and session._worker=None. Preserve that contract. The new stage check must bind the same registered startup, frozen release/selection/profile values, admission, session, permit, reservation and protection to the actual retained worker as durable binding and publication advance. Check current configuration before native effects and again at each publication boundary. A same-value replacement is insufficient.

2. Add one fixed coordinator module, provisionally `admitted_namespace_flow.py`, for the controller and child entry methods. Reuse `PrivatePipeController.attach_to_suspended_worker(pair, read_set, executable, arguments, working_directory, environment)` and existing ownership/cleanup mechanics. Consume controller authority before process work; retain its attempt, each returned pair/worker/channel and all custody before validation or another fallible call. `ControllerHandshake(channel, local_session, local_permit, primitives, native_worker)` receives the permit's identity token, while the controller registry retains the actual permit wrapper. Bind the exact read set, process creation time, fixed child source and generation. Fixed startup supplies classes, paths and key through its private inherited pipe; arbitrary caller callbacks, an independently constructed channel, or a supplied key cannot authorize this path.

3. Derive `inherited_readset.py` for a separate admitted-selection envelope. The current `controller_manifest(primitives, read_set, worker, root, case)` and `validate_manifest(payload, root, case, control_value, expected_manifest_sha256)` validate generated fixtures. Preserve them. The new envelope carries the approved release-manifest digest, selected choice/repository/revision and complete five-member names/sizes/digests, explicit profile/usage, snapshot identity and actual retained physical member identities with distinct inherited handles. Bind the whole canonical envelope to the same channel/source/process/generation; its digest is distinct from the approved manifest digest. Refuse omissions, extras, aliases and mismatches before content reads. Retain all adopted handles before querying flags or identity. The child validates controller-authenticated passive data; it does not manufacture a new REAL_APPROVAL.

4. Derive `owned_generation_protocol.py` for child-local issuance through the actual `WorkerBootstrap`. Use its challenge, live registry, owner-operation lock and `accept_initial_control(frame)` boundary. A begin must bind the admitted envelope; an initial empty cancel releases unread adoption, sends closed while the channel is live, then closes/revokes through the existing ordering. Neither path may materialize before begin. After readback, issue a private lease bound by issuance identity to this bootstrap, local permit, generation, exact adoption/read set/namespace, selection and profile. Recheck revocation and all bindings at publication. A constructed lease, ready-shaped namespace or exact class alone grants nothing. Never use `issue_generated_inputs` to authorize these buffers.

5. Derive `pinned_buffer_namespace.py` with an admitted materialization attempt retained before reading. The old adoption assigns its namespace only after `materialize()` returns; that method keeps partial chunks locally and clears buffers on failure. Preserve the generated behavior, but retain the new namespace, returned chunks and completed buffers before subsequent validation. Use the fixed `OwnedWin32Primitives`, `ReadSet`, `HandleRecord` and namespace types with their actual ownership registries. Keep exact size/hash/identity, bounded-read and single-use checks. No path reopening, loader callback or dictionary-of-bytes shortcut. Cleanup preserves the first error and uncertain references; read completion is not backend retirement.

Propose 16 focused controls through the actual new controller/child sequence and inert lower services: issued pre/post-stage success; foreign or copied startup/session/permit; changed release/profile after consumption; substituted worker/read set/source/creation time; independent channel/key refusal; changed envelope/selection/profile; missing/extra members; aliased inherited handles; physical identity or inheritance mismatch; materialization before begin; initial cancel without buffers; begin/cancel replay; copied lease/namespace refusal; short-read/hash failure with retained partial custody; revocation before publication with returned custody retained; and cleanup failure preserving the original exception. Use the isolated startup fixture modules and existing fixed fake transport. Do not seed private successful state to skip the new call sequence. Preserve old 81/39 assertions; list exact new IDs after source is written, without predicting passes.

Deliver complete source early, before copies, mechanical full diffs, actual derivative bindings, proposed tests and a short report. No harness is requested. Keep `_fixed_real_worker_start`, `activate_real_worker`, `acquire_real_read_namespace` and `activate_real_loader` unavailable until an actual approved fixed dispatcher supplies this route. Native authentication has not been established by this plan or the controller-only tests. Current real approval/release/profile globals remain absent; no caller-shaped witness fills that gap.

Source preparation only: no Python startup, imports, compile/tests, native calls, support/model/checkpoint/D2 access, physical journal/live-index/5179 access, network, production edits, Git operations or subagents. D1/D2 stay complete; D3/D4 remain separate decisions.

MEMBER-SCOPE-CORRECTION.md SHA256 50C711E6F54BA4D6729CC4887DD1A276966A7B7725B365CF707A5F8F92257A18
This addendum corrects the admitted-member scope in the frozen BRIEF.md (SHA256 86d66542bfcac53d74499bf8808edc2855406b026610452d9f42363615a668e6). That brief and SOURCE-INPUTS.json (a397a5c167a63bfcec1ce1f577a42f3225e2e4ea3da6b42e5e792c6ca3ec6dc4) remain unchanged.

The fixed resolver's MODEL_SPECS selects four files for tiny, base, small and medium, including vocabulary.txt. It selects five files for large and large-v3-turbo, including preprocessor_config.json and vocabulary.json. Bind the admitted envelope, physical read set, readback and child-local lease to the exact selected model's membership, names, sizes and digests.

For the admitted route, replace the opening instruction "five selected, verified buffers" with "the selected model's four or five verified buffers." In change 3, replace "complete five-member names/sizes/digests" with "the selected model's complete four- or five-member names/sizes/digests." These are the frozen brief's two fixed-five membership requirements; this addendum supersedes both. The existing generated five-member route remains unchanged.

Add a seventeenth proposed control: successful admitted four-file namespace issuance for a selected tiny/base/small/medium record containing vocabulary.txt, through the actual new controller-to-child sequence and inert lower services. It must verify exact membership and retained buffers, including the absence of preprocessor_config.json. Keep the existing success control for a selected five-file record.

Do not fabricate a preprocessor file or translate vocabulary.txt into vocabulary.json. Namespace issuance does not authorize a constructor or its filesystem fallback. Constructor eligibility, options and fallback refusal remain a separate unit.
